screened_candidates.citation: Czaczkes et al. 2017, Pheromone trail following in the ant Lasius niger: high accuracy and variability but no effect of task state

screened_candidates.citation: Chalissery et al. 2019, Ants Sense, and Follow, Trail Pheromones of Ant Community Members
screened_candidates.contamination: the abstract/search result exposed the direction and numerical distance outcomes of the Lasius niger trail-following bioassay

screened_candidates.citation: Koch & Czaczkes 2021, No specialist pheromone-ignoring ants in Lasius niger
screened_candidates.contamination: search metadata and an accessible literature table exposed the target pheromone-following rate before protocol freeze

discovery_conclusion.reason: Every high-relevance published candidate screened had target outcome semantics exposed in searchable abstracts, result snippets, or tables before a source-specific validation protocol could be frozen. Selecting any of them now as a blind promotion-grade holdout would misrepresent the evidence lifecycle.

criteria_contract_resolution.scientific_reason: The one-source target is subordinate to the mandatory blinding and independence criteria; no source may be selected by violating a mandatory criterion. A new dataset can satisfy the criteria prospectively after preregistration.

next_gate.purpose: Freeze the identity, apparatus, stimulus, sample-unit structure, primary endpoint, model prediction surface, RNG/simulation contract, statistical comparison, and any promotion rule for a new independent Lasius niger replication dataset before biological data collection or outcome access begins.
